claims.text: Overall wear resistance of the FeNiCrCoCu coating during high-temperature sliding is governed by coating grain size and grain-boundary density.
Microscopic deformation of the FeNiCrCoCu coating during high-temperature sliding is governed by coating grain size and grain-boundary density.
The baseline FeNiCrCoCu coating has a grain size of 10 micrometers.
A controlled annealing process can reduce the coating grain size from 10 micrometers to 1 micrometer.
Reducing grain size from 10 micrometers to 1 micrometer increases grain-boundary density.
Grain boundaries act as obstacles to dislocation motion in this coating.
Increasing the number of obstacles to dislocation motion enhances the coating's wear resistance.
Increasing the number of obstacles to dislocation motion reduces microscopic deformation.
Relative to the 10-micrometer baseline, the 1-micrometer coating will have improved wear resistance.
Relative to the 10-micrometer baseline, the 1-micrometer coating will exhibit reduced microscopic deformation.
The predicted effects apply at 500-700 degrees Celsius, a sliding speed of 1 meter per second, and a normal load of 10 newtons.
Below a grain size of 0.1 micrometers, other mechanisms may dominate.
Grain-boundary amorphization may dominate below a grain size of 0.1 micrometers.
Failure of the reduced-grain-size coating to show statistically significant improvements in both wear rate and microscopic deformation relative to the baseline would falsify the hypothesis.
